related-article.article-title: Less Can Be More by Circulating Tumor DNA Use in ERBB2-Positive Breast Cancer.

sec.title: Question
sec.p: Among patients with stage II to III ERBB2-positive breast cancer receiving neoadjuvant paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP), what are the long-term outcomes, and can ultrasensitive circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) monitoring provide a complementary measure of treatment response?

sec.title: Findings
sec.p: In this secondary analysis of the DAPHNe phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial including 98 patients, the 5-year recurrence-free interval was 98%. Baseline ctDNA was detected in approximately 90% of patients and cleared in 96% after THP; ctDNA was detectable at the time of the single local recurrence and cleared after resection.

sec.title: Meaning
sec.p: De-escalated THP produced excellent long-term outcomes, and near-universal ultrasensitive ctDNA clearance after treatment, warranting further validation of ultrasensitive ctDNA as a prognostic tool in this setting.

sec.title: Importance
sec.p: The neoadjuvant combination of paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) represents a promising abbreviated regimen for early-stage ERBB2-positive breast cancer, but long-term outcomes and the role of ultrasensitive circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) monitoring remain incompletely defined.

sec.title: Objective
sec.p: To assess 5-year outcomes and characterize ctDNA dynamics with an ultrasensitive assay in patients with ERBB2-positive breast cancer receiving neoadjuvant THP.

sec.title: Design, Setting, and Participants
sec.p: This study was a prespecified secondary analysis of the prospective, single-arm, investigator-initiated phase 2 DAPHNe nonrandomized clinical trial. Patients were enrolled in the DAPHNe trial from November 2018 to January 2020. The trial took place at a multicenter academic cancer center and affiliated community practices. Participants included patients with stage II to III ERBB2-positive breast cancer receiving neoadjuvant THP for 12 weeks. Ultrasensitive ctDNA analyses were performed in patients with available tumor tissue and serial plasma samples. The secondary analysis was conducted between between March 2023 and April 2025.

sec.title: Interventions
sec.p: Neoadjuvant THP administered for 12 weeks, followed by surgery and adjuvant therapy guided by pathologic response.

sec.title: Main Outcomes and Measures
sec.p: Main outcomes included 5-year event-free survival, recurrence-free interval (RFI), distant RFI, and overall survival. ctDNA detection and clearance were assessed using a whole-genome–based, tumor-informed ultrasensitive assay at 4 predefined time points (baseline, preoperative, postoperative, and late adjuvant).

sec.title: Results
sec.p: The overall trial cohort included 98 patients (median [IQR] age, 49.5 years [24.0-78.0 years]; 97 female patients [99.0%]; 1 male patient [1.0%]), with mostly stage 2 disease (91 patients [92.9%]) and hormone receptor–positive tumors (65 patients [66.3%]). With a median (IQR) follow-up of 5.2 (5.0-5.4) years, the 5-year event-free survival was 99% (95% CI, 97%-100%), the 5-year RFI was 98% (95% CI, 93%-100%), the 5-year distant RFI was 100% (95% CI, 100%-100%), and the 5-year overall survival was 99% (95% CI, 97%-100%). Among 57 patients included in ctDNA analyses, baseline ctDNA was detected in 51 individuals (89.5%). After neoadjuvant therapy, ctDNA clearance occurred in 49 of 51 patients (96.1%), with only 2 individuals (3.9%) remaining ctDNA-positive preoperatively; detectability remained low (<10%) during postoperative follow-up. One single patient experienced a local recurrence, with ctDNA detected at time of recurrence and cleared following surgical resection.

sec.title: Conclusions and Relevance
sec.p: In this secondary analysis of the DAPHNe nonrandomized clinical trial, neoadjuvant THP was associated with excellent long-term outcomes in patients with early-stage ERBB2-positive breast cancer. Ultrasensitive ctDNA analyses demonstrated high baseline detection rates and near-universal clearance after abbreviated neoadjuvant therapy, supporting further investigation of ctDNA-guided de-escalation strategies in this setting.

sec.title: Trial Registration
sec.p: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03716180

abstract.p: This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial evaluates 5-year outcomes and characterizes circulating tumor DNA dynamics in patients with ERBB2-positive breast cancer treated with 12 weeks of neoadjuvant paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: The use of ERBB2-targeted agents has reshaped the prognosis of ERBB2-positive breast cancer, with nearly 90% of patients with stage II to III ERBB2-positive breast cancer disease-free at 8 years after adequate systemic treatment.1 Thus, focus has gradually shifted to developing better-tolerated regimens through shortening the duration and reducing the intensity of traditional polychemotherapy regimens.2 De-escalation to Adjuvant Antibodies Post-pCR to Neoadjuvant THP (DAPHNe) was a single-arm prospective phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, in which patients with stage II to III ERBB2-positive breast cancer received an abbreviated neoadjuvant regimen comprising paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) for 12 weeks. More than half of the patients in the primary trial analysis achieved a pathologic complete response (pCR) at surgery (55 of 97 patients [56.7%]), and adherence rate to de-escalated antibody-only adjuvant therapy was 54 of 55 patients (98.2%), meeting the primary study end point.3 Here, we report updated 5-year follow-up from the DAPHNe trial and evaluate the prediction of clinical outcomes with an ultrasensitive circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assay.4,5

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: The trial protocol (Supplement 1) was approved at each of the 5 sites under the Dana-Farber/Harvard Cancer Center institutional review board. All patients enrolled between November 2018 and January 2020 and provided written informed consent per the Declaration of Helsinki principles. The Transparent Reporting of Evaluations With Nonrandomized Designs (TREND) reporting guideline was followed. This prespecified secondary analysis was conducted between March 2023 and April 2025.

In the phase 2 DAPHNe clinical trial, patients received neoadjuvant THP for 4 cycles, followed by surgery and adjuvant systemic therapy per physician discretion (with ongoing trastuzumab and pertuzumab but no further chemotherapy in case of pCR). Details of the trial design were previously reported, along with the primary end point.3 Prespecified secondary clinical end points included event-free survival (EFS), recurrence-free interval (RFI), and overall survival (OS); distant RFI was evaluated as a nonprespecified exploratory outcome. Detailed end point definitions are provided in the eMethods in Supplement 2.

Plasma samples were prospectively collected at 4 time points (Figure 1A). ctDNA was measured retrospectively using a tumor-informed assay using whole-genome sequencing of tumor and matched normal DNA to design personalized panels targeting up to approximately 1800 somatic variants.4,5 Analysts were blinded to patient outcomes and clinicopathological features during sample processing and ctDNA analysis (eMethods in Supplement 2).

caption.title: Serial Circulating Tumor DNA (ctDNA) Bar Plot With Annotation Heatmap of Highly Sensitive Detection of Preoperative ctDNA
caption.p: A, Workflow of plasma sample collection and ultrasensitive circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) panel (NeXT Personal panel; Personalis) preparation. The 7ultrasensitive ctDNA platform leverages tumor-informed information to achieve ultrasensitive cancer detection, longitudinal monitoring, and therapy monitoring from liquid-biopsy samples. Plasma was collected at baseline (<14 days before registration or cycle 1 day 1), before surgery (<6 weeks before surgery, and as close to surgery as possible; labeled post–neoadjuvant therapy [NAT]), at an early postoperative time point (<6 weeks after surgery, ie, in conjunction with postoperative physician visit; labeled after surgery), and at a follow-up time point (during the final 3 months of adjuvant ERBB2-directed therapy; labeled follow-up). B, Clinicopathological variables relating to preoperative and postoperative ctDNA detection in patients with ERBB2-positive breast cancer in the DAPHNe trial: ctDNA level (ppm tumor fraction); residual cancer burden (RCB) at surgery; clinical T and N stage at study enrollment; estrogen receptor (ER) status. THP indicates paclitaxel/trastuzumab/pertuzumab; WGS, whole-genome sequencing.

sec.p: Cohort characteristics were obtained from the primary trial. Race and ethnicity data were self-reported. P values were used to compare the ctDNA cohort and non-ctDNA cohort and were obtained via Fisher exact test for categorical variables and Kruskal-Wallis test for continuous variables. All tests were 2-sided, and the significance threshold was set at P < .05. SAS, version 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc), and R, version 4.4.2 (R Project for Statistical Computing), were used for the analysis.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Overall, 57 patients were included in the ctDNA analysis (eFigure 1 in Supplement 2). These patients had a median (range) age of 50.0 (26.0-76.0) years; 56 patients (98.2%) were female, and 1 patient (1.8%) was male. Most (53 patients [93%]) had stage II tumors, and 38 patients (67%) had hormone receptor-positive tumors. The cohort’s characteristics were representative of the overall DAPHNe population (N = 98; median [IQR] age, 49.5 years [24.0-78.0 years]; 97 female patients [99.0%]; 1 male patient [1.0%]), apart from a slightly lower mastectomy rate in the biomarker cohort (overall: 44 [44.9%] vs ctDNA cohort: 20 [35.1%]) (Table).

sec.p: At baseline, 51 of 57 (89.5%) had detectable ctDNA, with a median (IQR) detected level of 249 (67-1321) ppm and 16 (31%) of positive detections less than 100 ppm (Figure 1C). All patients with tumors of at least 5 cm (T3) or lymph node positive had detectable ctDNA at baseline, and patients with higher N stage showed significantly higher detectable levels by ppm (Figure 1B; eTables 1-2 in Supplement 2).

THP was highly effective at clearing ctDNA, with detectable minimal residual disease (MRD) rates of 3.5% (2 of 57) pre-surgery, 8.9% (5 of 56) postoperatively, and 4.9% (2 of 41) during final 3 months of adjuvant ERBB2-directed therapy (eFigure 2 in Supplement 2). A total of 51 patients had detectable ctDNA at baseline and available plasma samples before surgery. Among them, 49 (96.1%) cleared MRD during THP; only 2 patients had detectable MRD before surgery (eFigure 2 in Supplement 2). No significant association was observed between either baseline ctDNA, preoperative ctDNA, or the clearance of MRD with pathologic response at surgery (eTables 3-11, eFigures 2-3 in Supplement 2).

ctDNA was detected in 5 of 56 patients (8.9%) at the initial postsurgical time point, including 3 with residual disease and 2 with pCR at surgery. All 5 patients received adjuvant therapy, with 3 confirmed to clear ctDNA at a subsequent time point in response to treatment (eTable 12 in Supplement 2). At the late adjuvant time point, only 2 of 41 patients (4.9%) had detectable ctDNA levels. Notably, all positive ctDNA detections during the postsurgical surveillance period were identified at low concentrations (<100 ppm), highlighting the importance of ultrasensitive detection methods for accurate monitoring.

With a median (IQR) follow-up of 5.2 (5.0-5.4) years, no distant recurrences were observed in the 98 patients treated during the trial, consistent with a 5-year distant RFI of 100% (95% CI, 100%-100%) (Figure 2C). One local recurrence in the ipsilateral breast occurred in a patient 59 months after surgery; the patient had positive MRD at baseline, which cleared before surgery and remained negative at the immediate postoperative time point. Fresh plasma collected at recurrence showed ultrasensitive ctDNA detection (9.1 ppm), which converted to negative after tumor resection.

caption.p: A, Event-free survival (EFS), defined as the interval from study entry until invasive disease recurrence, new primary (breast or nonbreast), or death due to any cause. B, Recurrence-free interval (RFI), defined as the interval from the time of surgery until the occurrence of invasive local/regional recurrence, distant recurrence, or death due to breast cancer. C, Distant RFI (DRFI), defined as the interval from the time of surgery until distant recurrence or death from breast cancer. D, Overall survival (OS), defined as the interval from study entry until death due to any cause. A total of 98 patients were included in all curves. Five-year survival rates and 95% CIs were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier estimation method.

sec.p: The 5-year EFS was 99% (95% CI, 97%-100%) and the 5-year RFI was 98% (95% CI, 93%-100%) (Figure 2A-B). One patient developed a nonbreast second primary cancer (metastatic neuroendocrine tumor) 7 months after breast surgery, which ultimately caused patient death, leading to a 5-year OS of 99% (95% CI, 97%-100%) (Figure 2D).

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: The National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines currently recommend prolonged (18-24 weeks) neoadjuvant polychemotherapy with dual ERBB2-blockade.6 The findings reported in this secondary analysis of the DAPHNe nonrandomized clinical trial raise the hypothesis that favorable outcomes may be achieved with an abbreviated, de-escalated regimen. We demonstrated outstanding 5-year outcomes with THP for 12 weeks in a cohort in which most patients had stage II ERBB2-positive breast cancer, wherein 54 of 55 patients (98.2%) with pCR did not receive further adjuvant chemotherapy.3

The CompassHER2-pCR trial (NCT04266249) will determine whether outcomes for patients with pCR after THP are comparable to those after polychemotherapy. In CompassHER2-pCR, patients with stage II to IIIa ERBB2-positive breast cancer undergo neoadjuvant taxane-HP for 12 weeks, followed by no further chemotherapy after pCR. Preliminary results involving 2175 patients showed a pCR rate of 938 of 2141 (43.8%).7 Recurrence-free survival results are maturing and can establish THP as a standard de-escalated approach.

The availability of multiple potential treatment regimens provides the opportunity to tailor treatment according to disease response, which can be noninvasively tracked with ctDNA.8 In the DAPHNe trial, the use of an ultrasensitive assay significantly improved baseline ctDNA detection rates compared to standard assays,9,10 enabling baseline detection of ctDNA in approximately 90% patients with ERBB2-positive breast cancer, with most clearing ctDNA before surgery. These observations align with the lack of distant recurrences, though validation in larger cohorts is needed to establish ctDNA clearance as a favorable prognostic indicator. Importantly, in this cohort, the combination of an ultrasensitive MRD assay and a highly treatment-sensitive disease led to near-universal ctDNA detection at baseline and near-universal absence of ctDNA after treatment, rendering both time points uninformative for pCR prediction. Additionally, the ctDNA assessment time points in the DAPHNe trial were not optimal to test adaptive treatment strategies. ctDNA assessment after a single treatment cycle (eg, C2D1) may better discriminate treatment-sensitive from resistant tumors, as observed in the I-SPY2 trial.11

The lack of recurrences, with more than 5 years of follow-up, among the 6 patients with positive postoperative ctDNA detection (all in the ultrasensitive range, 0-100 ppm), speaks to the efficacy of adjuvant systemic therapy and to the sensitivity of the ctDNA measurement. Currently, the clinical threshold for actionable MRD and the prognostic significance of ultralow postoperative MRD detection remain undefined, warranting caution in interpretation.

sec.title: Limitations
sec.p: Limitations of this study include the nonrandomized design, the relatively small sample size of the ctDNA cohort, the lack of dense time points in the neoadjuvant plasma collection, and the lack of definitive postadjuvant therapy plasma sampling, which makes interpretation of the positive adjuvant time points more challenging.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: This secondary analysis of the DAPHNe nonrandomized clinical trial reinforces the potential role of de-escalated neoadjuvant THP for patients with stage II ERBB2-positive breast cancer. Postneoadjuvant ctDNA clearance may complement pCR status as a good prognosis biomarker in this setting, warranting further validation.
